Direct shear test on RSM-b soil; apparatus: direct shear (University of Notre Dame). Recorded: friction angle vs relative density.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 68 of the 75 points, and 3 are still under review. They have not yet been checked by a person. The test setup is incomplete: relative density Dr, unit weight, specimen height, normal stress, held constant, displacement rate are not reported.
:::

## Data

![angle of internal friction (direct shear) against relative density, SI units. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-ds-fc-22.png){.lightbox}

Peak angle of internal friction (direct shear) 52.06 deg at 0.9955 relative density; 52.1 deg at 1.001, the end of the record.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-22/observations.csv) (75 points: 2 plotted symbols, 67 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1: angle of internal friction (direct shear) in deg against relative density (dimensionless); the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-22/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on this figure (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 0.001981 in relative density, 0.06148 deg in angle of internal friction (0.1 percent of the peak). Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 68 of the 75 points; 3 are still under review (hollow in the plot) and 4 were settled against the scan. [Check the digitized points against the scan](../figures/index.qmd#check-fc-22).
